_readme: Eval seeds for It Stings. Run with `npm run eval` (all) or `npm run eval -- lovecats`. Each seed has notes on what a passing and a failing answer look like. Review the dumped results by hand against these notes after every change to the fingerprint, channel, scoring, or ranking logic. Seed 1 is the acceptance test.

seeds.title: The Lovecats
seeds.what_it_is: A post-punk band playing jazz on purpose: swung upright-bass shuffle, brushed drums, playful affected vocal that dissolves into scatting and cat noises, arch and flirtatious.
passing: Results share the jazz-shuffle-plus-playful-vocal-affectation axis, from multiple scenes and decades: swing revival (Squirrel Nut Zippers, Cherry Poppin' Daddies), jump blues (Louis Prima, Louis Jordan), lounge-influenced pop, arch British art-pop (Blur's music-hall moments, Madness, Ian Dury, The Divine Comedy), electro-swing (Caravan Palace, Parov Stelar).
At least a few picks a genre engine would never surface: a 1950s jump-blues side next to a 2010s electro-swing track next to an 80s art-pop single.
Every `why` names a concrete shared trait: the walking upright bass, the brushed shuffle, the vocal that slides into nonsense syllables, the wink in the delivery.
Spread across at least three decades and three scenes in the top 15.
failing: Other Cure singles. 'Close to Me' is not an answer; it is the absence of one.
Generic 1980s alternative rock that shares nothing but the decade and the label (Echo & the Bunnymen, Siouxsie, early New Order) unless the `why` names a real shared trait.
Any `why` that reads 'similar mood and style' or 'same era and genre'.

seeds.title: Golden Brown
seeds.what_it_is: Harpsichord waltz by a punk band: 3/4 with a recurring 4/4 bar that trips the meter, baroque-pop arpeggios, unhurried croon, sinister calm under a pretty surface.
passing: Harpsichord or harpsichord-like keyboard textures across eras: 60s baroque pop (The Left Banke, The Zombies' 'Time of the Season' family, early Bee Gees), 90s/00s chamber-pop, modern acts using the instrument.
Odd-meter or waltz-time pop with a calm, slightly menacing vocal.
Tracks whose `why` names the waltz lilt, the harpsichord arpeggio figure, or the pretty-surface-dark-undertow contrast.
failing: Other Stranglers songs, or generic punk/new wave from 1981.

seeds.title: Psycho Killer
seeds.what_it_is: Nervous, angular, minimal funk-punk: a stalking bass riff, jerky guitar stabs, a vocal that is twitchy and deadpan, breaks into French, and has a nonsense-syllable hook ('fa fa fa').
passing: Tracks with a stalking, repetitive bass figure and a twitchy deadpan vocal, from any scene: post-punk (Gang of Four, Wire), 2000s dance-punk (Franz Ferdinand, LCD Soundsystem), art-funk, new wave with a nonsense-syllable hook.
At least one cross-language or spoken/sung switch match, and at least one pick from outside 1976–1984.
`why` lines that name the bass riff, the vocal tic, the tension-without-release arrangement.
failing: Other Talking Heads songs (excluded by default).
A list that is just 'CBGB-era punk'.

seeds.title: Fever
seeds.what_it_is: Minimalism as seduction: finger snaps, a walking upright bass, a whisper of drums, and a cool, held-back vocal that never raises its voice. The arrangement is the hook.
passing: Tracks built on an almost-empty arrangement with snaps or claps and a restrained, sultry vocal, across eras: 50s/60s cool jazz vocals, trip-hop and downtempo (Portishead, Morcheeba), modern minimal pop (Billie Eilish's quieter cuts, Fiona Apple), neo-soul.
`why` lines that name the snaps, the walking bass alone under the vocal, the space in the mix.
Spread across at least four decades.
failing: Other Peggy Lee songs; a list of 'jazz standards' with no arrangement link.
Big-band or heavily orchestrated versions that share nothing but the songbook.

seeds.title: bad guy
seeds.what_it_is: Whispered, close-mic'd vocal over a bouncing sub-bass and a clicky minimal beat; cheeky and menacing; a spoken 'duh' punchline and a tempo-drop coda.
passing: Tracks with whisper-close vocals over sparse, bass-heavy production and a smirk in the delivery: 2010s alt-pop, some 90s trip-hop, minimal electro, art-pop with a spoken punchline.
At least a few picks from before 2010 that share the whisper-and-bass axis rather than the era.
`why` lines that name the whisper, the sub-bass bounce, the deadpan punchline, or the structural swerve at the end.
failing: Other Billie Eilish or Finneas-produced songs (same artist excluded; producer-only links are not a musical trait on their own).

seeds.title: Lone Digger
seeds.what_it_is: Electro-swing: a 1930s-style brass and clarinet riff and a swung vocal chopped over a four-on-the-floor house kick and a filtered bass; playful, cartoonish, dance-floor.
passing: Reaches backward to the source material (1930s–40s swing and hot jazz: Cab Calloway, Benny Goodman, Django Reinhardt) and sideways to swing-house/electro-swing peers (Parov Stelar, Tape Five) and to 90s big-beat or house tracks that sample swing.
`why` lines that name the clarinet/brass riff, the swung vocal over a straight kick, the sampled-78 texture.
Spread across at least three decades, including at least one pre-1960 recording.
failing: A list that is only 2010s electro-swing.
